message.content:
{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "name: CodeStyle

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

env:
  PHP_CS_FIXER_IGNORE_ENV: 1

jobs:
  psalm:
    name: Code Style
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Setup PHP ${{ matrix.php }} Environment
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-php
        with:
          os: ubuntu-latest
          php: 8.4

      - name: Cache Composer dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.composer/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-composer-${{ hashFiles('composer.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-composer-

      - name: Check Code Style
        run: composer phpcs:check", "rationale": "The workflow runs on push and pull_request with no dependency cache, so Composer packages are re-fetched on every run. Adding a Composer dependency cache before the code-style check preserves the same steps and coverage while speeding dependency restore on repeated runs. This matches the dependency-cache pattern (repeated fetching measurable, cache keyed on lockfile/runner, no equivalent cache already present) and is supported by the measured workflow example that adds actions/cache@v4 before dependency installation. The change is minimal, adds no privileges, secrets, deployment, or new external network access beyond the standard GitHub Actions cache service already used by checkout/setup actions.", "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]}
